chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: When a man prostrates, then intends to stand up, he should not knead his hands in the ground, but he should extend his palms without placing his buttocks on the ground.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to rise from prostration in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the physical mechanics of rising from sujdah, emphasizing a dignified, smooth transition rather than a forceful push-off. In Shia fiqh, this specific posture is often linked to the concept of *khushu* (humility) and distinguishes the prayer of the Ahl al-Bayt from other traditions, ensuring the body remains poised and ready for the next movement without breaking the flow of devotion.
